The repo pins Node 20.11 in .nvmrc (engines is >=20.11 <21), so a Node 18 install will fail with an engines error. It uses pnpm 9 only, never npm or yarn, since those write their own lockfiles and CI rejects them. Seeding with scripts/seed-demo also needs Postgres running and DATABASE_URL set before `pnpm start`.
Action: In ~/code/acme-platform run `nvm install` then `nvm use`, check `node -v`, then `pnpm install`, and then check what Postgres and DATABASE_URL you have before seeding.

Yes, with the default loader, next/image requests go to /_next/image on our Next server, which fetches the remote image, resizes and converts it, and caches the result. So the first request for each avatar size hits our node process, and later ones are served from the cache. If you want avatars to bypass the server, you'd use `unoptimized` or a custom loader that points straight at the CDN. The production build I just checked resolved the cdn.acme.dev avatars through /_next/image.
Action: No code change; I can check whether next.config.ts sets a custom loader or `unoptimized` if you want to confirm what we do today.

The database is MySQL 8, so I'll write this in MySQL 8 syntax: paid invoices only, grouped by org_id and month for the last 12 months, with a running total per org via a window function (`SUM(...) OVER (PARTITION BY org_id ORDER BY month)`). The usual rule is that queries filter by org_id; this one is a cross-org finance rollup, so it groups by org_id instead, and I'll note that in a comment. Money is integer cents with fractional line quantities, so line amounts should be rounded to whole cents before summing; I'll check the schema in apps/api/migrations for the exact column names and whether invoices store a total or I need to sum lines.
Action: Read the invoice tables in apps/api/migrations, then write tools/sql/ monthly revenue rollup .sql returning cents (plus currency if the schema has one).

Two separate causes. The prerender error is the Clerk key check: production builds fail if a dev key (pk_test_) is used, so the Vercel production env for the release branch has a dev publishable key and needs the live key; that's an env var, not a code change. The hydration warning is a timezone mismatch on the due date (the server formatted 12:42 PM, the client 8:42 AM), which is fixed by formatting the date on the client in useEffect or by suppressHydrationWarning on the time element.
Action: Check which Clerk publishable key variable the production build reads and tell you what to set in Vercel (I can't see its env), then fix the due date column using the client-side formatting approach.

Uploads don't go through the API. The browser calls POST /v1/uploads to get a presigned S3 PUT URL (valid 300s), PUTs the file directly to S3, then calls POST /v1/uploads/:id/complete. Progress needs XMLHttpRequest (xhr.upload.onprogress) rather than fetch, and Lena wants a progress bar. I haven't looked at how an expense references an uploaded file, so I'll check the expense schema and endpoint for that.
Action: Read the expense form and the existing upload code, add a PDF file field that runs the three-step upload with an XHR progress bar, and attach the completed upload to the expense.

The signing needs a secret, so it has to run on the server and never in client code; I'll put it in apps/web/lib/share-link.ts as server-only. The link will carry the invoice id, an expiry timestamp and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over those two values, checked with a constant-time comparison. Since the preview component is probably a client component, it'll call a server action or route to get the link. I don't know yet which env var holds the signing secret, so I'll check.
Action: Look at the preview component and existing env config, write share-link.ts with sign and verify using node:crypto, wire the copy-link button to it, and add tests for valid, tampered and expired links.
